verdict.rationale: Microsoft's first-party docs list an "Extended Security Updates (ESU) program for Windows 10," which matches extending security update coverage on an installation. The evidence is only a single headline mention, scoped to Windows 10, with no detail on how an individual enrolls, how many years it covers, or what it costs. Missing for 10: documented enrollment/enablement steps for individual power-users, coverage duration and eligibility details, applicability beyond Windows 10, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
